### Observed differences

- In the later window, activity A20 almost always leads to A22 (about 99 in 100 cases), whereas in the earlier window it led to A30 (about 40), A31 (about 33) and A36 (about 28) and never to A22. [DIR001, LAG001]
- In the later window, activity A21 no longer leads to A25 (about 1 in 100, down from 100 in 100); instead it leads to A30 (about 36), A31 (about 33) and A36 (about 31). [DIR002, LAG004]
- In the later window, activities A30, A31 and A36 each lead to A25 in about a third of their outgoing transitions, whereas in the earlier window they led to A22 in about 29–38% of transitions and never to A25. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- In the later window, A21 and A22 occur earlier in the trace (mean position about 0.53 and 0.38, down from 0.62 and 0.47), while A30, A31 and A36 occur later (mean position about 0.59, 0.58 and 0.59, up from about 0.41). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- For each pair (A21,A30), (A21,A31), (A21,A36), (A22,A30), (A22,A31) and (A22,A36), the order reversed: in the earlier window the second activity preceded the first in 100% of cases; in the later window the first activity precedes the second in about 99% of cases. [REL001–REL006]
- The distance between A20 and A22 changed from 4 steps (100%) to 1 step (99%), and the distance between A21 and A25 changed from 1 step (100%) to 4 steps (99%). [LAG001, LAG004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a reordering of the process: in the later window, A21 and A22 are executed before A30, A31 and A36, whereas in the earlier window they were executed after them. A20 now leads directly to A22, and A25 is reached later, via A30/A31/A36, instead of directly from A21. This is directly shown by the successor changes (DIR), the position shifts (POS), the pairwise order reversals (REL) and the lag changes (LAG). The number of qualifying items (22) is far above the 0.42 expected by chance, and the main items have full support in both windows. A competing explanation that cannot be fully ruled out is that some of the lag items with very low support in the later window (only 2 traces) reflect sampling noise, but the core ordering change rests on items with 200 traces in both windows.

Other differences: none beyond the reordering described.
